name: Give a convincing 30-second introduction
blurb: What you say when someone asks what you do. Most people improvise badly every time; thirty minutes of preparation makes you memorable for years.
steps: Write down what you actually do in one plain sentence, with no jargon and no job title that means nothing outside your industry.
Add the “so that” — the outcome or the problem you solve — because that is the part people remember.
Add one concrete, specific detail or example. Specificity is what makes it stick.
End with something that invites a reply rather than closing the conversation.
Cut it to under 30 seconds spoken aloud, then rehearse until it sounds like speech rather than recitation.
Build three variants: for a peer, for a stranger at a party, and for someone who might hire you.
tips: Vagueness is the killer. “I work in consulting” tells nobody anything.
Practise out loud, not in your head. Written-sounding sentences are obvious when spoken.
proof: Three people can accurately repeat what you do after hearing it once.
